ending: The book closes while Jake is still competing in Nevermore. He has completed four challenge dungeons, accumulated an 80 percent combined score multiplier, and entered the Never-Ending Journey as a courier with three lives. His House reward includes a private, time-dilated alchemical domain and ten bound attendants. The Sword Saint has reported a Grand Champion result, but Dina, Sylphie, and the Fallen King remain in separate challenges. Temlat is dead by his own request after destroying his world's ruling order, and Jake has decided against taking another formal student soon. Valdemar's offer of Valhall membership remains unanswered, Artemis still intends a private conversation, and Minaga continues to watch Jake closely. Vesperia has support to travel toward the 93rd universe, while Miranda, William, and Sandy continue their separate preparations and investigations. Neither Jake nor the Malefic Viper understands the origin-linked power that enabled the victory over Valdemar's image.
in_short: Jake and his party pause their regular Nevermore climb to attempt solo challenge dungeons. In the Colosseum, Jake rises from a restricted level-zero fighter to sole Grand Champion, killing Valdemar's image after an unexplained bloodline survival response. He then completes the Test of Character and Minaga's Endless Labyrinth, while his victories attract Valdemar, Artemis, and many other gods. In the House of the Architect, Jake develops ten varied creations and recruits Temlat as his first student. Temlat evolves into a plague remnant of wrath, destroys his world's oppressive ruling order, then asks Jake to consume him. Jake earns a 20 percent House multiplier and a permanent private alchemical domain, bringing his total challenge multiplier to 80 percent. The book ends as he begins the courier-based Never-Ending Journey with three lives, leaving his party's reunion, divine affiliations, Vesperia's migration, and the nature of his origin power unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne entered Nevermore with Sylphie, Dina, the Sword Saint, and the Fallen King. The group has been advancing through the dungeon while competing for points, with Jake continuing to develop as the Malefic Viper's Chosen.

Jake's party completes floor 70 and reaches another Nevermore City floor while still holding the points record for that stage. Because later floors offer larger rewards and every available challenge dungeon is now open, the five members agree to spend roughly ten internal years on solo trials before reuniting. Jake and the Sword Saint enter the Colosseum, while Dina, Sylphie, and the Fallen King choose different challenges. The Colosseum strips Jake down to a normalized level-zero body, confiscates his equipment, limits his skills, and gives him ten lives. His bloodline, titles, and perception remain active, leaving him unusually capable. He befriends the spear user Owen and meets Polly, an elven sorcerer who offers information. Jake climbs the early ranks without a loss, relying almost entirely on kicks. Experiments with predatory presence become Fear Gaze, a nonlethal technique that can freeze weak opponents and disrupt spell control. The crowd gives him the unwanted name Doomfoot as he approaches the true gladiator ranks.

Jake reaches Gladiator without losing a life and begins weekly ranked bouts, daily show matches, and systematic archery practice. He reveals arcane-enhanced strikes, buys light boots, and continues advancing far faster than ordinary competitors. His promotion to Veteran Gladiator comes through an agreed scoring bout against the Benevolent Monk. Although Jake draws blood first and technically wins, the monk's soul-based defense and attacks leave him convinced that a lethal rematch would be far harder. Jake responds by buying katars and protective equipment suited to his counterattacking style. He also notices Owen hiding lightning magic while Polly develops both magic and basic melee skills. After ten Veteran Gladiator victories, Jake defeats the undefeated dwarven earth mage known as the Earthborn Faithful in his Master Gladiator promotion bout. The opponent surrenders, though the post-match rank notification has not appeared by the end of chapter 16. Jake remains unbeaten with all ten lives intact, while Carmen and the Sword Saint are also noted for strong Colosseum performances.

Jake advances through Warlord and Paragon while refining archery, transmutation, and stable arcane defenses. In a lethal rematch, he defeats the Benevolent Monk after a severe exchange, but an unidentified entity briefly speaks through the dying image and leaves its purpose unclear. Jake then learns that Colosseum opponents are system-assisted level-zero images based on other beings. Owen admits he is the son of one of the champions and has concealed the distinctive lightning inherited from his father. Away from the arena, Mira returns to the Willowwood clan with the authority of Duskleaf's disciple. Publicly revealed as Mistress Dawnleaf, she claims the clan to protect it and reunites with her mother Delia and three younger siblings. She refuses to rule their choices and instead arranges formal status, protection, and freedom of movement. Back in the Colosseum, Jake completes ten Paragon victories and prepares for his promotion to Champion with his archery still largely concealed.

Jake's Champion promotion opponent is Gudrun, the Valhallian Valkyrie and Valdemar's wife. Her formations, prepared equipment, and deceptive tactics initially control the arena, but Jake reveals his bow, wounds her at range, defeats her in melee, and grants her requested warrior's death. Champion rank opens the Gauntlet of the Grand Champion against seven other champions. Owen asks Jake to spare his father, the Lightning Monarch, while Polly asks him to kill the Archmage who coerced her through threats against her parents. Jake exhausts the Lightning Monarch's enhancement and persuades him to surrender, leaving Owen with an unwanted expectation of succession. He then kills the Archmage's image with a prepared arrow barrage. Jake's third opponent is the heavily armored Necromancer. His opening plan pierces and blasts apart the champion's armor, but the death knight survives the apparent killing wound. By the end of chapter 32, Jake is poisoned and injured as the unresolved first fight continues through spreading miasma.

The Undying General kills Jake in their first gauntlet fight, costing him one life, but Jake returns with a plan and destroys the image in their rematch. He then defeats the Phoenix Queen after her apparently fatal loss triggers a fiery reconstruction and she surrenders while weakened. Jake fights the Lord of the Hunt in a prolonged archery duel and wins by cutting her bowstring with a concealed final arrow. She identifies herself as Artemis, recovers her divine memories, and offers Jake limited hunting instruction after he declines her invitation to become her chosen. Jake then faces Umbra in a shadow-favored arena. His bloodline perception defeats her concealment, clones, and shadow domain, and she surrenders after warning him about the reigning Grand Champion. Jake's last gauntlet opponent is the Battlemaster, revealed as the retired Warmaster. The weapon master cycles through legendary armor, traps, explosives, and a broad arsenal, but Jake turns the wire trap against him and forces a surrender. Jake becomes a Grand Champion with nine lives remaining. He may now leave, accept escalating show matches, or challenge the Warrior for sole status. Based on the title and the available warnings, Jake believes the final opponent is Valdemar.

Jake challenges Valdemar's image and spends repeated lives learning an opponent whose direct axe attacks cannot be safely blocked. Valdemar retains divine memories and explains that recognition, surrender, or death may end the match. On Jake's final life, an unstable arcane body boost lets him inflict serious wounds, and Fear Gaze creates an opening that earns Valdemar's recognition. The intended challenge is already cleared, but Valdemar still brings down a final overwhelming strike. Jake releases a suppressed survival response from his bloodline. For several seconds he gains extraordinary control, creates a void, converts sand into usable energy, and coordinates a fatal counterattack. Valdemar dies, and Jake becomes the sole Grand Champion. The Colosseum awards a 25 percent score multiplier, a powerful title, and an emblem for normalized virtual duels. The bloodline episode then leaves Jake's senses badly distorted. The Sword Saint separately becomes a Grand Champion by defeating Umbra, but his transcendence backlash persists, and he cannot clear Valdemar.

The Malefic Viper cannot fully explain Jake's victory, though he suspects Jake briefly released a normally suppressed bloodline state and spent accumulated origin energy to survive it. Artemis and the true Valdemar begin traveling to Nevermore after receiving records of their images. Jake partially recovers and enters the Test of Character, a sequence of scenarios in which he may guide or take control of another person's body. He responds according to his own judgment, sometimes refusing to intervene and sometimes removing threats directly. During the trial his senses recover, his archery improves, and Fear Gaze becomes the mythical Primal Gaze of the Apex Hunter. Jake completes one hundred scenarios with an excellent result, gaining a 10 percent multiplier, while Jacob and Arnold each earn 20 percent through very different but more consistently suited approaches. About fifty gods have gathered to see what Jake's achievements may signify. When Jake criticizes the trial, its altered exit offers a redacted destination, which he accepts.

The redacted exit places Jake before a gathering of major gods. Valdemar offers him membership in Valhall, but Jake postpones any answer at the Malefic Viper's direction. The apparent hostility between Valhall and the Malefic Order is exposed as a coordinated deception intended to complicate Yip of Yore's plans. Artemis and Jake agree to speak privately later, while Jake's aura contest with Valdemar strengthens his public reputation. Jake then enters Minaga's Endless Labyrinth. His perception lets him map routes far faster than normal, though later sections add shifting walls, teleporters, illusions, lethal shortcuts, and increasingly strong gatekeepers. He spends one reset fighting a B-grade guardian for experience, then avoids similar battles. Sylphie is revealed to possess an unusual wind-guided navigation talent that also lets her advance rapidly. On his final attempt, Jake reaches section 214 and deliberately tests the next guardian rather than continue. The run ends with a 25 percent multiplier and a portable labyrinth, bringing his combined challenge multiplier to 60 percent.

Outside Jake's run, William investigates false karmic control on the Nahum homeworld, Sandy demonstrates a hunger-guided way to choose wormhole exits, and Vesperia declares her intention to travel from the Endless Empire to the 93rd universe. The other true royals support Vesperia after learning of Jake's feat against Valdemar's image. Jake enters the House of the Architect, where ten diverse creations determine his result. The House requires fresh work and records the methods behind each creation. Its confidential architect reveals herself as Nevermore, the bound god who sustains the living dungeon, and promises to shield Jake's submissions from outside observation. Jake counts their meeting as his first creation and explores portal worlds for materials, tasks, and possible students. In a futuristic world, a lost-pet assignment turns out to concern an escaped half-elf servant. Jake detects the servant's curse energy and recruits him for alchemy training instead of returning him to his owner.

The half-elf identifies himself as Temlat and chooses Jake's offer of training over enslavement. Jake develops his hatred curse, teaches him unconventional alchemy, and sends him through a lethal solo exercise in a war-torn world. Temlat returns stronger after spreading his curse through a settlement until its inhabitants turn on one another. Jake recognizes the danger of that preferred path but continues to emphasize self-direction. Alongside the apprenticeship, Jake creates a stimulant that draws more stored curse energy from Eternal Hunger, repeatedly attempts grimoire construction, and improves his stealth. He eventually produces a unique profession grimoire and evolves his concealment into a legendary mobile skill after infiltrating a capital unnoticed. After nine months in the House, Jake has four completed creations and several additional projects planned. Temlat approaches C-grade while focusing increasingly on curse proliferation, psychological destabilization, and revenge.

Jake expands the range of his House submissions with a coercive ritual, a corrupted elemental spirit orb, a perpetual arcane marble made with a trace of origin-linked energy, and a hemonecrotic poison. Nevermore values the marble's unprecedented records but refuses to explain the primeval energy involved. Jake also begins acidcraft as a final avenue for diversity. Temlat reaches level 199 and receives an evolution quest requiring him to affirm or reject the source of his hatred. Jake refuses to rush the decision, and the quest directs Temlat back to his homeworld.

Temlat evolves into a Cursed Plague Remnant of Wrath, retaining enough identity to pursue his own definition of justice. His plague spreads through the city-world, directing wrath toward rulers and other powerful classes while causing mass violence and death. He kills the woman who owned him, rejects the curse energy released by her death, and devastates the planet's oppressive order over five days. After sparing weaker survivors, Temlat asks Jake to end him while his mind remains his own and to preserve his records through consumption. Jake complies, and Eternal Hunger consumes him. Temlat's death removes the plague and curse from the surviving infected population. Jake returns to the House, submits Temlat's path as a creation, and reflects that he should have discussed consequences more clearly with his student. He then completes an adaptable arcane acid, leaving only one final submission before evaluation.

Jake's final poison becomes the ancient Malefic Blackheart poison through direct intervention from the Malefic Viper, completing all ten House submissions. Nevermore's evaluation places the perennial arcane marble, the profession grimoire, and Temlat's path above his other work. She confirms that Temlat would otherwise have died before reaching C-grade and judges Jake's teaching exceptional because it enabled the student to choose both his path and its end. Jake earns 86,109 Nevermore points and a 20 percent multiplier. His reward includes a legendary Mark of the Architect and a private, time-dilated domain configured as an alchemical growing space with ten attendants. With four challenges complete and an 80 percent combined multiplier, Jake enters the Never-Ending Journey. The new trial assigns him courier work in a modern city, with harder deliveries and political complications unlocked through reputation. Failed jobs disappear, death costs one of three lives, and the book ends with this final challenge only beginning.
